card.name: Open parenthesis after a dose amount
card.fires_on: The opening parenthesis right after a dose in mg, where the unit count (such as one capsule or 2 tablets) is about to be given. It also fires on 'to' in dose equivalence phrases.

modes.label: Parenthesis before unit count
modes.description: The '(' after a mg dose that introduces the number of capsules, tablets or injections.
modes.example: 750 mg<< (>>one capsule) three times daily for up

modes.label: Equivalence phrase
modes.description: The word 'to' in a dose equivalence, just before a single-unit amount.
modes.example: may be required to provide pain relief equivalent<< to>> 1 mg of parenteral morphine

card.writes: It promotes words meaning one or a single item (one piece, one pair, ONE), so it prepares the model to write 'one' as the count.
card.plain: It fires when a dose in mg is followed by a bracket that will say how many tablets or capsules, often just one.
